title: Linkability of GPS data across time and sources
description: Regular GPS coordinate transmissions can be linked to create movement patterns, and may be correlated with other data sources to build comprehensive profiles of the child's activities and locations.
assumptions: Backend stores historical GPS data; multiple data sources may exist

title: Direct identifiability through location data
description: GPS coordinates directly identify the child's physical location, potentially revealing home address, school, daily routines, and other sensitive personal information.
assumptions: GPS data is precise enough to identify specific locations

title: Lack of authentication for data transmission
description: Without proper authentication, it may be unclear whether GPS data originated from the legitimate child's device or was spoofed by an attacker.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be weak or absent
uncertainty_note: Depends on implementation of authentication in the app

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data
description: GPS coordinates received by the backend could be accessed by unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or insecure APIs.
assumptions: Backend stores GPS data; security controls may be insufficient

title: Aggregation of location data over time
description: Regular GPS transmissions enable the backend to aggregate location data, building detailed movement profiles that reveal habits, routines, and sensitive locations visited by the child.
assumptions: Backend retains historical GPS data for analysis

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: The child (and potentially guardians) may not be fully aware of the frequency, purpose, or extent of GPS data collection, especially if consent mechanisms are unclear.
assumptions: Privacy notices may be complex or not child-friendly

title: Non-compliance with children's privacy regulations
description: Collection of children's location data may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws if proper consent, data minimization, and security measures are not implemented.
assumptions: App operates in jurisdictions with children's privacy protections
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation

title: Location pings can be linked to identify individual users
description: Location history data written to the store can be linked across time and sessions to create comprehensive movement profiles of individual users, enabling tracking of daily routines, habits, and associations.
assumptions: Location data includes sufficient granularity (coordinates, timestamps) to enable user identification through pattern analysis

title: Location data can directly identify individuals
description: Location history is highly identifying personal data that can reveal home addresses, workplaces, medical visits, and other sensitive information about specific individuals.
assumptions: Location pings are associated with user accounts or device identifiers

title: Location data collection may exceed minimality principle
description: Continuous location ping storage may collect more personal data than strictly necessary for the app's functionality, representing an avoidable data disclosure.
assumptions: The app's core functionality does not require persistent storage of all location pings
uncertainty_note: Depends on app's actual functional requirements - may be justified if location history is a core feature

title: Users may be unaware of continuous location logging
description: Users may not be fully aware that their location is being continuously written to persistent storage, especially if consent was obtained for a different purpose or scope.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate the extent of location data collection and storage

title: Users lack control over stored location history
description: Once location pings are written to the store, users may have limited ability to delete, modify, or control how their location data is used and retained.
assumptions: The system does not provide user-facing controls for location data management

title: Excessive location data disclosure to geofencing engine
description: The Mobile App Backend forwards location pings to the Geofencing Engine. This represents an explicit disclosure of sensitive personal data (location). The threat is whether all location data being forwarded is strictly necessary for geofencing functionality, or if more granular/precise data is being disclosed than required (violating data minimization principle).
assumptions: Location pings contain precise GPS coordinates or similar location data

title: User identification through location patterns
description: The Geofencing Engine receives location pings that could be used to identify specific users through their movement patterns, even if explicit identifiers are not included. Location data is inherently identifying when combined with temporal patterns and known user zones.
assumptions: Location pings are associated with user accounts or can be correlated to identify individuals

title: Linking location data with other user data
description: The Geofencing Engine may link incoming location pings with other user data (profile information, alert history, etc.) creating a more comprehensive user profile than users may expect or consent to.
assumptions: Geofencing Engine has access to or can correlate with other user data stores

title: User unawareness of location data forwarding
description: Users may not be fully aware that their location data is being forwarded to a separate geofencing engine process, or may not understand the implications of this data transfer for their privacy.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain internal data flows between backend components

title: Unauthorized disclosure of zone definitions
description: Configured zone definitions (home, school, friend's house locations) stored in DS2 could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the data store is compromised or the data flow is intercepted. This reveals sensitive location information about family members.
assumptions: Data store has appropriate access controls; data flow is protected in transit

title: Identifiability through location data
description: Zone definitions containing home, school, and friend's house locations can identify specific individuals and their daily routines. If exposed, this data enables identification and profiling of family members.
assumptions: Zone definitions contain specific location identifiers

title: Data misuse for tracking or profiling
description: Zone definition data read by the Geofencing Engine could be misused beyond its intended purpose (geofencing alerts) for continuous tracking, behavioral profiling, or surveillance of family members.
assumptions: Process P2 has appropriate purpose limitations; data is not logged or shared beyond intended use

title: Unawareness of location data processing
description: Family members may be unaware that their location preferences (zone definitions) are being read and processed by the Geofencing Engine, or may not understand the privacy implications of this data flow.
assumptions: Users have been informed about data processing activities

title: Non-compliance with location data regulations
description: Processing of location-based zone definitions may require specific legal basis under GDPR or similar privacy regulations. The data flow may not have proper consent mechanisms or legal justification documented.
assumptions: Applicable privacy regulations require explicit consent for location data processing

title: Location data linked to child identity
description: Geofencing notifications link the child's location movements (zone entry/exit) to their identity, creating a persistent link between location data and personal identity that could be exploited if intercepted.
assumptions: Notifications contain identifiable information about the child

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data
description: If the notification flow is intercepted, sensitive location information (when child enters/exits defined zones) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Communication channel may not be fully secured

title: Deduction of child's routine and patterns
description: From the timing, frequency, and zones of notifications, an attacker could deduce the child's daily routine, school schedule, home address, and behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Multiple notifications over time create pattern data

title: Child unaware of location tracking
description: The child may not be aware that their location is being continuously monitored and that notifications are being sent to the parent, violating their right to know about data collection.
assumptions: Child may not have been informed about geofencing monitoring

title: Child lacks control over notification data
description: The child has no ability to control, modify, or opt out of the geofencing notifications being sent to the parent, limiting their agency over personal data.
assumptions: Child cannot configure or disable geofencing alerts

title: Linkability of registration data to child tracking data
description: Parent registration data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) can be linked to subsequent location tracking and activity data, creating a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and habits.
assumptions: System stores and correlates registration data with ongoing location/activity data

title: Direct identification of parent and child
description: Registration data includes directly identifying information (parent name, child name, DOB, school) that can uniquely identify both individuals.
assumptions: Data is stored in a form that preserves direct identifiers

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive child information
description: Child's personal information (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or insecure transmission.
assumptions: Data transmission and storage may have security vulnerabilities

title: Aggregation of registration data with other child data
description: Registration data can be aggregated with location tracking, activity logs, and other data sources to create detailed behavioral profiles of the child.
assumptions: System collects and stores multiple data types about the child

title: Parent unawareness of data collection scope
description: Parent may not fully understand what data is being collected, how geofence zones are used, or how long data is retained.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not clearly explain all data uses

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Collection of child data (name, DOB, school, location zones) may not comply with regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws requiring parental consent and data minimization.
assumptions: System may not have adequate compliance measures for child data
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation details

title: Linkability of child profiles to accounts and locations
description: Child profile data stored in DS2 can be linked to specific family accounts and geofence zones, enabling correlation of children's identities with their locations and family relationships.
assumptions: Data store maintains relationships between account IDs, child profiles, and geofence zones

title: Identifiability of children through stored profile data
description: Child profile data stored in DS2 may contain or enable identification of individual children, especially when combined with account and geofence information.
assumptions: Child profiles contain personally identifiable information or can be linked to real identities

title: Unauthorized disclosure of stored personal data
description: Account, child profile, and geofence zone data stored in DS2 could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Data store has security controls that could be compromised

title: Excessive data collection and storage
description: The backend may store more account, child profile, or geofence data than strictly necessary, violating the minimality principle for personal data collection.
assumptions: Data minimization practices may not be fully implemented
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual data fields stored - would need schema review to confirm

title: User unawareness of data storage practices
description: Users may not be fully aware of what account, child profile, and geofence data is being stored, how long it's retained, or what purposes it serves.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain data storage practices

title: Limited user control over stored personal data
description: Users may have limited ability to access, modify, or delete their account, child profile, and geofence data stored in DS2.
assumptions: Data management interfaces may not provide full user control

title: Location data linkability to child identity
description: The child's location data transmitted to the parent can be linked to their identity and other personal data, enabling tracking of movements and activities over time.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient precision to identify the child's whereabouts

title: Child identifiability through location patterns
description: Location history and current location data can reveal the child's identity through movement patterns, frequented locations, and behavioral signatures.
assumptions: Location data is precise enough to identify individual movement patterns

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child location data
description: Location data could be intercepted during transmission or accessed by unauthorized parties through the mobile app backend, exposing the child's whereabouts.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or backend may have access control vulnerabilities

title: Aggregation of location history reveals sensitive patterns
description: Accumulated location history data can be aggregated to reveal sensitive information about the child's routines, habits, social connections, and frequented places.
assumptions: Location history is stored and can be queried over time

title: Child unaware of location tracking and sharing
description: The child may be unaware that their location is being tracked and shared with the parent, violating their right to know about data processing affecting them.
assumptions: Children may not understand or be informed about location tracking features

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Location tracking of minors may not comply with regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws requiring specific consent mechanisms and data minimization.
assumptions: System may not have appropriate age verification or parental consent mechanisms
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific implementation details not provided in the DFD

title: Location history linkable to specific children
description: Location history data stored in DS1 can be linked to identify specific children when retrieved by the backend, enabling tracking of individual movement patterns and routines.
assumptions: Location data includes timestamps and coordinates that can be correlated with child identities

title: Location data reveals child identity and patterns
description: Retrieved location history can directly identify children and reveal sensitive information about their daily routines, school locations, and home addresses.
assumptions: Location history is stored with sufficient granularity to identify individuals

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location history
description: If the Mobile App Backend (P1) is compromised or has inadequate access controls, location history retrieved from DS1 could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Backend has access to sensitive location data and may have security vulnerabilities

title: Aggregation of location data reveals sensitive patterns
description: When the backend retrieves and processes location history, aggregation with other data could reveal sensitive patterns about family routines, school schedules, and behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Backend may combine location data with other user data for analytics or features

title: Potential non-compliance with children's privacy regulations
description: Retrieval and processing of children's location history may not comply with regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws if proper consent and safeguards are not in place.
assumptions: Location history involves children's data subject to special privacy protections
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific implementation of consent and data handling practices

title: Linkability between parent, secondary guardian, and child
description: The invitation flow creates linkability between the parent (EE1), the secondary guardian being invited, and the child whose location is being shared. This enables correlation of identities and activities across multiple parties.
assumptions: The invitation contains identifiers that can link these parties together

title: Direct identification of parent and secondary guardian
description: The parent's identity and the secondary guardian's identity are transmitted to the backend, making both parties directly identifiable in the system.
assumptions: Identity information is included in the invitation request

title: Disclosure of child location sharing intent
description: The backend receives and processes information about which parties are being granted access to the child's location data, disclosing sensitive sharing relationships.
assumptions: The backend stores or logs the invitation details

title: Unawareness of data processing by secondary guardian
description: The secondary guardian may not be fully aware of what data will be processed about them or the child when accepting the invitation, or the extent of location data sharing.
assumptions: Consent and transparency mechanisms may be insufficient

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Sharing child location data with additional guardians may require specific consent mechanisms under regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K, which may not be properly implemented.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for child location data sharing apply
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific regulatory requirements

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's live location
description: The child's live location data transmitted to the secondary guardian could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission, or the wrong guardian could receive the data if access controls fail.
assumptions: Transmission occurs over network; access controls exist but may be bypassed

title: Location data aggregation with other child data
description: The secondary guardian could aggregate the received live location data with other personal information they have about the child, creating a more comprehensive profile that increases privacy risks.
assumptions: Secondary guardian may have access to other child-related data

title: Child identifiability through location data
description: Live location data can be used to identify the child, especially when combined with other data points or if the location is unique (e.g., home address, school).
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient precision to identify the child

title: Child unawareness of location sharing
description: The child may not be aware that their live location is being shared with the secondary guardian, or may not understand the implications of this data sharing.
assumptions: Child may not have been informed about location sharing practices

title: Linkability of aggregated analytics to user profiles
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics shared with advertising partner may be linkable to individual user profiles when combined with other data sources the partner possesses, enabling cross-service tracking and profiling.
assumptions: Advertising partner maintains user profiles from other services and can correlate analytics data

title: Re-identification from aggregated analytics data
description: Even aggregated analytics data may allow re-identification of individual users through statistical inference, especially when combined with external datasets held by the advertising partner.
assumptions: Aggregation level may not provide sufficient anonymity; partner has access to complementary datasets

title: Unauthorized disclosure to third parties beyond advertising partner
description: Data shared with advertising/analytics partner may be further disclosed to additional third parties without user consent or knowledge, expanding the data sharing ecosystem beyond the original agreement.
assumptions: Partner's terms of service allow sub-licensing or data sharing with affiliates

title: User unawareness of analytics data sharing
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their usage and engagement data is being shared with external advertising partners, particularly if privacy notices are buried or unclear.
assumptions: Privacy policy exists but may not be prominently displayed or clearly explained

title: Potential non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Sharing usage analytics with advertising partners may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, or purpose limitation are not implemented.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements apply to this app's user base; consent and data handling practices may be insufficient
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific jurisdiction and consent implementation

title: Location data linkability to child identity
description: The child's location data sent in check-in/SOS messages can be linked to their identity and combined with other data flows to create a comprehensive movement profile.
assumptions: Child's identity is known to the system and location data is stored/processed

title: Direct identifiability from check-in messages
description: The manual check-in/SOS message with location directly identifies the specific child sending it, making them identifiable from this data flow.
assumptions: Message contains or is associated with child's identity information

title: Attributable data evidence for child actions
description: The check-in/SOS message can be attributed to the child as the sender, creating non-repudiation evidence of their location and actions at a specific time.
assumptions: System logs and attributes messages to specific child accounts

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child location data
description: The Mobile App Backend could be compromised or have access control issues, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive child location and check-in data.
assumptions: Backend stores or processes location data with potential access vulnerabilities

title: Location data aggregation revealing movement patterns
description: Multiple check-in/SOS messages over time can be aggregated to reveal the child's movement patterns, routines, and frequently visited locations.
assumptions: System retains historical location data from multiple check-ins

title: Child unawareness of location data implications
description: The child may not fully understand what location data is being collected, how it's stored, or who can access it when sending check-in/SOS messages.
assumptions: Child users may lack full comprehension of privacy implications

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Collecting and processing location data from children may violate regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws if proper safeguards aren't in place.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdictions with child privacy protections
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation details
